To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy required to produce unit net optical density on a film is constant over a wide range of beam qualities for CaWO4 screens.

the optical density of an intensifying screen depends on the energy absorbed by the screen and that the energy absorbed by an intensifying screen is a constant for all x-ray beam qualities used in medical radiography.

the energy absorbed in the phosphor of a CaWO4 intensifying screen is constant within experimental error for a range of beam quality and that a family of characteristic film curves for a film-screen system can be reduced to one curve expressed as a function of the energy absorbed in a screen.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of a new method of measuring and evaluating energy absorption in x-ray intensifying screens, which will be of value to those interested in the physical basis of x-ray image production and the design of screen systems.
the evaluation of the absorbed-energy constant for CaWO4 x ray intensifying screens and its application to the characterization of x ray film.
the evaluation of the optical density of x-ray intensifying screens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the absorbed-energy constant, which has been shown to be a constant for a particular film and CaWO4 screen combination, is useful for predicting the optical density for variable x-ray beams.
the absorbed-energy constant is a useful and accurate parameter to describe the optical response of a film-screen system to x rays.
the energy which must be deposited in a calcium tungstate screen to produce unit optical density on the film is constant within experimental error for a range of diagnostic beam qualities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absorbed-energy concept provides an excellent basis for characterizing and predicting the response of CaWO4 screens for diagnostic x-ray applications.
the energy absorbed in the screen is the primary variable in determining the net optical density on a film.
the absorbed-energy constant is a fundamental property for the CaWO4 screen-film system, independent of the beam quality and the phosphor loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy absorbed in a CaWo4 x-ray intensifier is independent of x-ray beam quality.
the energy which must be deposited in the CaWO4 phosphor to produce a unit optical density is a constant over a wide range of x-ray beam qualities.
the absorbed-energy constant is a useful quantity for predicting the optical density for any beam condition.
